brief.headline: Push for a ₹32.69 L/yr price correction to match our lowest laminate rates, leveraging our 9.72% revenue share and offering faster payment against their 81d cash cycle.

priceAsk.summary: Align all laminate SKUs to our best-in-class prices and close the ₹32.69 L annual gap.
priceAsk.target: ₹290.00/KG benchmark (the rate Shrinath Roto Pack Pvt Ltd delivers); eliminate the ₹32.69 L/yr excess we currently pay GEEP.
priceAsk.basis: Three top SKUs run 1.4% to 6.3% above ₹290.00/KG — the lowest price we already pay for comparable laminates. The market line for BOPET film substrate sits at 171.60 ₹/kg, well below their finished-laminate pricing, so there is room.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to cut payment terms from 30 Days After Receipt to 15 days in exchange for a proportional price discount of roughly 4.38%.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to 15-day terms frees ₹1.16 Cr of our working capital; accelerating payment by 15 days is worth approximately their 4.38% effective borrowing cost, so trade speed for that price cut.

brief.financialLeverage: GEEP's 1.1% net margin sits half the 2.1% peer median, and their 6.6% return on capital trails the 14.6% peer benchmark — they run tight. Their 81d cash-conversion cycle is 35 days longer than the 46d peer median, so cash velocity matters to them. We represent 9.72% of their ₹291.36 Cr revenue (₹28.31 Cr spend), making us a top-tier account they cannot afford to lose. The CRISIL BB+ / Stable rating carries an "Issuer Not Cooperating" flag, signalling stale data and hidden risk. Debt is moderate at 0.57x equity and interest coverage is adequate at 4.12x, but ₹-1.64 Cr free cash flow and compliance red flags (GST delays, EPF delays, pending legal cases) mean we should press terms and working capital, not squeeze margin to the point of supplier failure.

evidence.point: We overpay ₹32.69 L per year versus the best laminate price we already secure elsewhere.
Top SKU LM ELECTRAL MD 21.80g LS 08 costs us ₹308.30/KG — 6.3% above the ₹290.00/KG Shrinath benchmark.
Our ₹28.31 Cr annual spend is 9.72% of their ₹291.36 Cr revenue — a material customer relationship.
Their 81d cash cycle runs 35 days longer than the 46d peer median, tying up working capital they need to free.
Their 1.1% net margin is half the 2.1% peer median, leaving little room for deep price cuts without risking stability.
BOPET substrate import benchmark sits at 171.60 ₹/kg, well below their laminate sale prices, confirming conversion-margin headroom.

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed converter with ₹2611.64 Cr revenue and B (64/100) health score — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets already in our supply base.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant (₹16492.00 Cr revenue, C health 54/100) that both makes film substrate and converts to laminates — can backstop GEEP at scale.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter (₹222.04 Cr revenue, D health 31/100) specialising in pharma blister and sachet laminates — direct second-source fit.

risks: GEEP holds 67% of our Laminates volume (₹28.31 Cr) — over-concentration means any supply hiccup hits hard; urgently qualify a second converter.
The CRISIL BB+ / Stable rating is on an "Issuer Not Cooperating" basis, so financials may be stale or incomplete; treat their stability as uncertain.
Their 1.1% net margin and ₹-1.64 Cr free cash flow leave no buffer — pushing too hard on price could tip them into distress and disrupt our supply.
GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, and pending legal cases flag operational and compliance stress; monitor delivery reliability closely during any renegotiation.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹32.69 lakh a year more than our best laminate price — let's work together to close that gap and explore faster payment terms that free up cash for both of us.
